expected.tagline: Dangerous Land is a first-person real-time strategy game combining settlement management, army command, exploration and combat. Develop your settlement, recruit an army and stand alongside your soldie
expected.description:
Become the ruler of a medieval settlement and lead your people to victory.

Dangerous Land is a first-person combination of real-time strategy, tower defense and action. Build and develop your settlement, gather resources, recruit soldiers and prepare for the dangers ahead.

You don't observe your army from above. You are part of the action. Manage your settlement, give orders to your units, develop its infrastructure, then stand alongside your soldiers and personally take part in the battle.

SURVIVAL CAMPAIGNDefend your settlement against waves of enemies.

Expand your settlement, gather resources, recruit and upgrade units, and prepare the right defenses. Each wave presents a greater challenge, so you must make good use of your available resources and prepare properly for the incoming attack.

Your goal is to survive all the waves and protect the Town Hall at all costs.

CONQUEST CAMPAIGNDo you prefer a slower pace and more time for planning?

The Conquest Campaign offers a completely different way to play. Set out for new islands, develop your settlement and prepare to attack enemy settlements. You don't have to fight through a series of predetermined waves. You decide when you are ready to begin your conquest.

However, you can't wait forever. Enemy settlements develop as well, strengthen their forces and eventually begin sending increasingly powerful attacks against you.

The Conquest Campaign is still in development and introduces many new mechanics and possibilities. It includes new defensive structures, the Fame system that allows you to unlock new possibilities, mysterious altars and circles that provide new abilities and bonuses, as well as a map that allows you to plan your next conquests.

BUILD AND DEVELOP YOUR SETTLEMENTYour settlement is the foundation of your entire army. Gather resources and develop your infrastructure to expand its capabilities. Build structures for production, resource storage, army recruitment, technological development and settlement defense.

Upgrade the Town Hall to unlock new possibilities that will help you with both economic and military development.

EXPLORE THE WORLDBeyond the borders of your settlement lies a dangerous world filled with resources, places to discover and enemies.

Set out on expeditions to gather the resources you need, discover new locations and capture strategic points.

RECRUIT AND COMMAND YOUR ARMYYour soldiers are essential both for defending your settlement and conquering new territory. Recruit different units, develop their capabilities and give them orders.

You can arrange your troops into formations and command them from a first-person perspective, watching the battle up close. At the same time, you can step onto the battlefield yourself and fight alongside them.

TAKE PART IN THE FIGHTIn Dangerous Land, you are not just a commander watching the battle from a safe distance.

You can step onto the battlefield yourself and fight alongside your soldiers.

Use a sword, shield, bow and potions to support your army and personally fight your enemies. Gain experience points and develop your skills to become an increasingly effective warrior.

UPGRADE YOURSELF AND YOUR ARMYDevelop your capabilities as you progress through the game. Upgrade buildings, create upgrades for yourself and your units, and conduct research to increase the capabilities of your settlement and army.

Adapt your development to the situation and prepare for the challenges that await you on your expeditions and in battle.

Build your settlement. Raise your army. Step onto the battlefield.

Will you survive the coming waves, or set out to conquer enemy settlements?

Dangerous Land is also on Steam and is free there. Open the store page and press Play Game to add it to your library.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. Dangerous Land needs roughly 1.0 GB of free disk space.

set.tagline: Build the walls, command the army, then stand in front of the charge yourself.
set.description: Dangerous Land combines a medieval settlement builder with first-person combat. Recruit units, develop defenses and protect the Town Hall through Survival missions, or prepare your own offensives in the still-developing Conquest campaign.

min.cpuText: Intel Core i3-7100 3.9 GHz or AMD Ryzen 3 2200G
min.notes: Windows 10/11 64-bit; Steam does not state a required graphics API.

set.launcherInstall.note: The complete Windows game is a paid Steam Early Access purchase; a separate free demo is offered on the same store page. Buy and install the full game through Steam, then use PlayBound Locate. No verified one-click standalone package exists.

qualityBar.verdict: The appeal is leaving the strategy table to defend the walls you just paid to build.

set.longDescription:
Dangerous Land asks you to do two jobs that are usually kept separate. You build a medieval settlement, manage its resources, recruit soldiers and choose where defenses should go. Then, when enemies appear, you can stand beside those soldiers with a sword, shield or bow. The change of perspective makes the planning personal. A gap in the wall is not an abstract inefficiency when you are the one trying to hold it.

The Survival campaign is the clearer route through the current Early Access build. Waves get harder, and keeping the Town Hall standing gives every investment a simple purpose. You can upgrade buildings, train units and research improvements, but every resource spent on growth is a resource not spent on the next attack. The Conquest campaign changes the pace. Instead of waiting for fixed waves, you develop a settlement and choose when to move against other islands, while rival settlements develop and eventually strike back. The developer is explicit that this mode is still being expanded. That is a useful warning for anyone expecting a complete second campaign today.

The game's first-person angle is its selling point and its complication. You can give orders and arrange formations, then switch from manager to participant when fighting starts. That makes a successful defense feel earned in two different ways: the workers gathered enough, and you managed to survive with the army they equipped. It also means the interface has to carry settlement management and combat without the distance of a conventional overhead strategy camera. Players who enjoy that hybrid should find plenty to inspect. Players looking for a polished, complete RTS may prefer to wait while Early Access continues.

The old PlayBound Draft copied the full Steam store description and incorrectly told people to install the game free. Steam currently sells the full game and offers a separate demo. The main catalog record is for the paid Early Access title. Steam lists Windows 10/11 64-bit, a Core i3-7100 or Ryzen 3 2200G, 4 GB RAM, GTX 750 or R7 370 and 1 GB storage as its minimum; its recommended tier raises those parts and asks for 8 GB RAM and 2 GB storage. Those figures are now in the structured hardware section rather than only pasted as prose.

Steam lists Dangerous Land as single-player. There is no verified native multiplayer, PlayBound party mode or dedicated server, and the developer page does not advertise controller support. A first-person camera by itself is not evidence of a gamepad-friendly UI, so PlayBound should not add a controller badge without a tested profile. The game remains a Draft while we assess whether the hybrid play and unfinished Conquest content meet the platform's bar. Its most interesting moment is simple: the defense you designed has to withstand an attack while you are standing inside it.
set.whyWePickedIt: Dangerous Land has a strong mechanical hook: a settlement defense game played from the commander's boots. Survival mode gives the building decisions immediate stakes, while Conquest suggests a broader campaign if development continues. We are keeping its Early Access state, paid ownership and single-player scope clear during testing.
set.thatOneThing: You approve the defense budget in the morning and personally discover its flaws when the attackers arrive.

installSteps.text: Buy the full Dangerous Land game on Steam and install it from your library. A free demo is available separately on the same store page; it is not the full game.
After Steam finishes installation, use PlayBound Locate to select the existing game installation. Keep Steam available for ownership and updates.
Start with the Survival campaign to learn settlement production and defensive waves. Conquest is still being developed in this Early Access release.

firstPlaySteps.text: Gather resources, strengthen the Town Hall approach and recruit a small force before the first Survival wave. Practice moving from build orders into first-person combat.
